validity.recommendation: none -- existence, classification, and non-duplication confirmed; see status_reviews for the open status question
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed real via two mutually independent origins: (1) Great Basin's own project microsite (expansion2024.greatbasingtcprojects.com, an Oracle APEX/ORDS session-based site -- the sheet's stored session URL had expired; refetched a live session), which describes the '2024 Expansion Project' as three named segments (Truckee Canal, Silver Springs, Kingsbury) in Douglas/Lyon/Storey Counties, NV totalling 3.41 mi; and (2) FERC's own Federal Register record, five notices under Docket No. CP23-466-000, all titled 'Great Basin Gas Transmission Company ... 2024 Expansion Project': Notice of Application (2023-10738, filed 2023-05-01, states the project in the applicant's own words: 0.25 mi new 20-in loop/Storey Co., 2.88 mi 10-in->20-in replacement/Lyon Co., 0.28 mi new 12-in loop/Douglas Co. -- summing to exactly 3.41 mi and exactly matching the sheet's Diameter='10, 12, 20'), Notice of Scoping (2023-13265, 2023-06-22), Notice of Schedule for EA (2023-14987, 2023-07-14), Notice of Availability of the EA (2023-26542, 2023-12-04, FERC staff found no significant environmental impact), and a Sunshine Act meeting notice (2024-08783, 2024-04-23) listing the docket as Certificates agenda item C-5 for the Commission's 2024-04-25 open meeting. CLASSIFICATION: correct as 'transmission' gas pipeline -- filed under NGA sections 7b/7c (interstate gas transmission jurisdiction), described throughout as looping/replacing pipe on Great Basin's Carson and South Tahoe Laterals to add firm transportation capacity for two existing shippers. DUPLICATE CHECK against the other 4 rows in the Great Basin cluster researched concurrently (P7856 Main Line 900 mi operating; P7858 Gabbs Lateral NASF Relocation 32.6 mi; P7859 2026 Expansion, FERC CP25-209-000, 2.32 mi, Lyon/Washoe Counties; P7860 2028 Expansion, FERC PF26-5-000 pre-filing, 6 counties): P7857's docket (CP23-466-000, filed 2023-05-01, Douglas/Lyon/Storey Counties, 3.41 mi) is a distinct FERC proceeding from all of them -- not a duplicate of any sibling row. NOTE: the brief's own EIA pre-matched-candidate section for P7857 pointed to the EIA 'Great Basin Expansion Project' record (docket CP25-209-000, in-service 2028) -- verified this is a MISATTRIBUTION: CP25-209-000 is actually P7859's 2026 Expansion docket (see cross_row_leads for P7859, already independently confirmed by that row's own shard); EIA carries zero rows matching P7857's real docket CP23-466 in any release. LENGTH/DIAMETER/LOCATION spec is confirmed at tier=high (2 independent origins: operator's own site + FERC/Federal Register) -- see fills.

cross_row_leads.facts: Great Basin's own 'Who We Are' page states the overall Great Basin system is approximately 898 miles ('Great Basin's transmission system consists of approximately 898 miles of pipeline'), running from the Idaho/Oregon/Nevada border area to the Nevada-California border, plus an LNG peak-shaving facility near Lovelock, NV. P7856 (Main Line) is recorded at 900 mi -- close but not identical to the operator's own 898-mi figure; worth reconciling (rounding, or a small segment attributed elsewhere in the cluster, e.g. laterals not counted in the 898-mi trunk figure) when building/reviewing the P7856 shard.

verifications.note: FERC Sunshine Act meeting notice (issued 2024-04-18, meeting 2024-04-25) lists 'C-5 ... CP23-466-000 ... Great Basin Gas Transmission Company' under the Certificates agenda -- the last independently dated evidence found of this docket being active, i.e. the certificate order was up for Commission consideration/vote at that meeting. The notice itself warns 'Items listed on the agenda may be deleted without further notice,' so this is evidence the matter reached the Commission's calendar, not proof an order actually issued that day.

FERC staff's Environmental Assessment (issued 2023-12-04) found the proposed project, with mitigation, 'would not constitute a major federal action significantly affecting the quality of the human environment' -- a positive/no-objection staff finding, consistent with a routine, uncontested small expansion likely headed toward approval, not one that stalled for cause.

As of this sweep, Great Basin's own current projects page (root site, live, re-fetched) still lists 'Great Basin 2024 Expansion Project' as one of its four current/recent projects (alongside Gabbs Lateral NASF Relocation, 2026 Expansion, 2028 Expansion) -- the operator has not removed it or marked it cancelled/withdrawn, but the page also carries no explicit 'completed'/'in-service' marker either way.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: RESOLVES the brief's central question on the '2024' label: it is the project's OWN designation, used identically by the operator and by FERC in all five Federal Register notices ('2024 Expansion Project' / 'Proposed 2024 Great Basin Expansion Project'), filed 2023-05-01 (ProposalYear/Month) -- i.e. '2024' names neither the proposal year nor a GEM-invented label, but the operator's/FERC's own target year for the project (consistent with standard FERC pipeline-project naming, which typically names a project for its intended construction/in-service year, not its filing year). CANNOT independently confirm whether the certificate was actually granted or the pipe actually built/placed in service: the only citable federal agency record trail (5 Federal Register notices, all one origin under the addendum's multiple-notices-from-one-agency rule) runs 2023-05-01 through the 2024-04-25 Sunshine Act meeting listing and then goes silent -- but FERC's post-certificate compliance filings (the actual order, and any construction-completion/in-service notice) are filed directly to the eLibrary docket, not published in the Federal Register, and FERC eLibrary (elibrary.ferc.gov) is a JS-only Angular SPA that returns no scrapable content via curl on any endpoint tried (search, guessed REST paths, legacy docket_sheet.asp -- all return only the static app shell). Escalation attempted beyond FERC/EIA/SEC per the orchestrator's specific suggestion: Nevada PUC's own docket search (puc.nv.gov/dockets/, /search/) is also a JS-rendered Episerver Find application with no server-side result content reachable via curl -- tried the dockets landing page and a direct query string, both returned only the JS app shell. PHMSA's annual-report operator-mileage page 403'd. Southwest Gas Holdings' FY2024 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2025; same origin family as Great Basin's own site per the corporate-parent rule) discusses Great Basin's FERC-jurisdictional rate case activity in 2024 in general terms but never names this specific project, docket, or either lateral -- silence, not evidence either way. Given (a) continuous, unbroken forward regulatory progress from filing through a positive-finding EA to a Commission agenda listing over 2023-05 to 2024-04 (the opposite of the pattern the dormancy rule targets, which is silence/no-progress), (b) no withdrawal, denial, or cancellation notice found anywhere, and (c) the operator's own site still carrying the project as current -- I am NOT applying the 2-year proposed->shelved dormancy rule here; doing so would very likely misclassify a small, uncontested, positively-reviewed expansion that probably was approved and built as an abandoned one. Equally, I am not flipping Status to 'operating'/'confirm' without a source that actually states completion/in-service -- that would overclaim. Verdict left 'unclear' with the full dated evidence chain recorded here; GEM's own LastUpdated for this row is 2025-10-21 (per the current GGIT snapshot), i.e. GEM itself revisited this row about a year ago and still recorded 'proposed' -- consistent with this also being a hard-to-resolve case for that review, not a simple oversight. Recommend a follow-up check with actual FERC eLibrary/CourtLink-style docket access (not curl-scrapable) or a Nevada PUC records request to find the order and any in-service filing.
